A quiet pause in a busy day. At ORA Toucheer Head Spa, take a moment to close your eyes, let your shoulders drop, and leave the rush of the day at the door. With gentle botanical scalp care, and a quiet space to rest, you can take a breath and let the tension of the day ease.

## ORA at a glance

ORA Head Spa & Wellness is the Waltham, Massachusetts head spa of TOUCHEER, a herbal scalp care brand founded in 1998. Rituals run 60 to 90 minutes, one therapist to one guest, with prices from $169 to $189.

## Three rhythms. One exhale.

Every ritual begins with a gentle consultation. Simply choose the feeling you would like to return to.

### Pure Reset

In 60 minutes, our Pure Reset ritual cleanses oil and styling residue, rebalances the scalp and releases tightness for guests with congested roots, priced at $179. Best for oily scalps, product build-up and anyone who wants a lighter, cleaner scalp.

### Vital Glow

In 75 minutes, our Vital Glow ritual deep-cleanses, feeds the scalp with botanical care and smooths the hair for guests who want softness and shine, priced at $169. Best for dry, dull or weighed-down hair that needs nourishment.

### Deep Stillness

In 90 minutes, our Deep Stillness ritual extends cleansing and slow massage from scalp to neck and shoulders for guests who need to decompress, priced at $188.99. Best for screen fatigue, shoulder tension and a full reset.

### Rituals and prices

All rituals are one-to-one and include the scalp check, botanical cleanse and quiet rest. Prices in USD.

## Quiet words from our guests

## Head spa FAQ — Waltham, MA

The questions guests ask before their first ritual: what a head spa actually does, how often to come, what to prepare and what it costs.

### What is the difference between a head spa and a regular shampoo?

A head spa is a 60 to 90 minute scalp treatment, not a wash-and-go. At ORA the therapist checks your scalp, cleanses it with warm botanical water, massages scalp, neck and shoulders, then leaves you to rest. A regular shampoo cleans hair in minutes; a head spa treats the scalp.

### How often should you book a head spa session?

It depends on your scalp. Oily or congested scalps usually settle with a 60 minute Pure Reset every three to four weeks, while dry or sensitive scalps often prefer a 75 minute Vital Glow less often. Your therapist suggests a rhythm after the first scalp check.

### Can I book if I am pregnant or have a sensitive scalp?

Yes, with a note at booking. We keep pressure light, skip strong essential oils and heat on request, and adjust the ritual to what feels comfortable. Tell us about pregnancy, allergies, scalp conditions or recent treatments so the therapist can adapt — and check with your doctor if unsure.

### What should I do before my first head spa visit?

Come as you are: there is no need to wash your hair, and skip heavy styling products if you can. Arrive five minutes early so we can run the scalp check, talk through the 60, 75 and 90 minute rituals and choose what suits you. Robes, towels and the herbal cleanse are provided.

### Do I need an appointment at ORA?

Yes — rituals are by appointment. Choose a service and a time on our booking page, where the calendar shows live availability. Walk-ins depend on the day’s schedule, so booking ahead is the only way to secure a specific day, time and therapist.

### How much does a head spa at ORA cost?

Rituals are $179 for 60 minutes (Pure Reset), $169 for 75 minutes (Vital Glow) and $188.99 for 90 minutes (Deep Stillness). Gift cards run from $25 to $1,000, and the annual membership is $288 with 10% off every ritual, one complimentary ritual and 20% off retail.

### Where is ORA Head Spa and when is it open?

ORA is in Waltham, Massachusetts, and open Monday to Sunday from 10:00 to 21:00. Booking, gift cards and membership are handled on myoraspa.com, and the rituals take place in the Waltham studio.

### What happens during an ORA ritual, step by step?

Every ritual follows five steps: a short consultation, a close scalp check, a warm botanical cleanse, slow massage from scalp to neck and shoulders, then a quiet rest. The three rituals differ in time and depth, not in sequence.
